final_candidates.decision_summary: Highest EVEscape antibody-escape score (z=0.906) with full ESM-1v plausibility (z=1.0). Charge-reversal at this surface loop position should disrupt m102.4-class binding while leaving the ephrin-binding face intact.
Second-highest escape score (z=0.833) with high PLM plausibility (z=1.0). Glycine introduction adds loop flexibility that can reduce antibody avidity without obvious fitness cost.

Strong escape score (z=0.874) but only moderate PLM plausibility (0.604) suggests some fitness cost. N→D charge introduction at an antibody-facing loop is a classic escape pattern, retained as third pick.

stop_reason.detail: All 4 tool calls and 4 rounds used; final Top-3 is stable across evidence dimensions.

history.rationale: Glu509 lies in the m102.4 antigenic face of the RBP head adjacent to the ephrin-binding rim; a charge flip is a common neutralization-escape mechanism with limited receptor-contact overlap.
Charged-substitution on a surface-exposed loop near the receptor-binding face could perturb antibody contact while likely tolerable; pending structural and PLM evidence.
Weak escape score (0.446); charge-reversal at a surface position offers little predicted benefit here.

rejection.reason: Weak escape score (0.446); charge-reversal at a surface position offers little predicted benefit here.

history.rationale: Tyr511 is a surface-exposed aromatic residue within the epitope region; removing the bulky side chain can reduce antibody contact while keeping the ephrin-B2 pocket intact.

Aromatic-to-Ala substitutions often strongly disrupt antibody paratope contacts, but Y may also contribute to receptor-binding surface; needs phenotype and structure evidence before ranking above E509K.
Solid escape (0.799) and neutral PLM; alanine substitution of a large aromatic is riskier for local stability but remains viable backup.
Decent escape score (z=0.799) but removing a large aromatic side chain carries elevated risk to local fold/receptor-adjacent contacts. Out-ranked by safer top-3 options.

rejection.reason: Decent escape score (z=0.799) but removing a large aromatic side chain carries elevated risk to local fold/receptor-adjacent contacts. Out-ranked by safer top-3 options.

history.rationale: Conservative change at an epitope-loop residue that disrupts m102.4 hydrogen bonding while preserving local backbone compatibility.
Conservative charge-neutralizing change; moderate escape potential, low disruption risk.
Moderate escape (0.724) with neutral PLM; conservative Asp→Asn kept as a lower-priority backup.
Lowest-ranked remaining candidate; conservative D→N change gives only modest predicted disruption. Insufficient evidence to justify keeping it in the active pool.

rejection.reason: Lowest-ranked remaining candidate; conservative D→N change gives only modest predicted disruption. Insufficient evidence to justify keeping it in the active pool.

history.rationale: Gly514 sits in a surface loop over the receptor-binding rim; adding a side chain can sterically hinder mAb binding with modest structural perturbation.
Small tolerated substitution, modest predicted effect on antibody binding.
Good escape (0.790) and neutral PLM; conservative substitution, retained in pool.
Escape score (z=0.790) is below the top candidates, and PLM scored it only as neutral-plausible without structure evidence. No differentiating evidence to keep it active.

rejection.reason: Escape score (z=0.790) is below the top candidates, and PLM scored it only as neutral-plausible without structure evidence. No differentiating evidence to keep it active.

history.rationale: Asn516 is an epitope-adjacent glyco-competent surface position; substitution here may introduce local charge change without touching core ephrin-contact residues.
Potential N-linked glycosylation-loss or charge change near epitope; worth evaluating with evolution and phenotype tools.
Second-highest escape score (0.874) but ESM-1v plausibility is reduced (0.604), slightly lowering confidence in structural/functional tolerance.
High escape score (0.874) but only moderate PLM plausibility (0.604); combined with null MSA support this keeps it third rather than second.

Strong escape score (z=0.874) but only moderate PLM plausibility (z=0.604), suggesting a possible fitness cost; retained as third pick. A N→D charge introduction at an antibody-facing loop is a classic escape mutation pattern.
Trp503 is a large epitope residue near the mAb contact surface; replacement reduces hydrophobic packing with the antibody but is riskier for receptor-adjacent folding.
Drastic Trp-to-Arg change may strongly alter antibody contact but risks destabilizing a folded core region; keep pending structure evidence.
Low escape score (0.559) despite neutral PLM; a bulky Trp→Arg replacement in a conserved region is not justified by the evidence.

rejection.reason: Low escape score (0.559) despite neutral PLM; a bulky Trp→Arg replacement in a conserved region is not justified by the evidence.

history.rationale: Loop residue adjacent to the receptor rim; glycine can shift loop conformation to evade antibody contact while preserving the ephrin-binding residues.
Glycine at a loop position is often tolerated but effect on escape is unclear.
Strong escape score (0.833) combined with neutral PLM plausibility (1.0); glycine is a mild, structurally tolerated substitution in a surface loop region.
Strong escape score (0.833) and PLM 1.0; weak MSA applicability (0.24) slightly reduces confidence given Gly at 515 is unobserved in shallow homologs.

Second-highest escape score (z=0.833) with high PLM plausibility; glycine at this loop position may add local flexibility that further reduces antibody avidity. MSA evidence is inapplicable (coverage 0.24) and does not outweigh direct phenotype evidence.
Conservative-size charge reversal on the epitope face; moderate escape potential but near structural constraints and a cysteine partner.
Charge flip on surface residue; moderate escape potential.
No phenotype prediction available (app=0) and reduced PLM plausibility; insufficient evidence to keep it active.

rejection.reason: No phenotype prediction available (app=0) and reduced PLM plausibility; insufficient evidence to keep it active.

history.rationale: Removal of a polar side chain in the epitope loop; modest antibody-contact reduction expected with low structural risk.
Good escape score (0.823) but mildly below-neutral PLM (0.839); retained as backup behind the top three.
Good escape (0.823) and decent PLM (0.839), but conservation entropy 0.950 at 513 is the lowest of the pool, hinting this position may be functionally constrained.

Good escape score (z=0.823) but a conservative T→A change offers less binding-surface disruption than top candidates, and it is out-ranked overall. Dropped in favor of higher-scoring, higher-confidence options.

rejection.reason: Good escape score (z=0.823) but a conservative T→A change offers less binding-surface disruption than top candidates, and it is out-ranked overall. Dropped in favor of higher-scoring, higher-confidence options.

history.rationale: Charge flip on the RBP surface within the antigenic region; candidate for escape with preserved folding, but farther from the m102.4 core epitope.
Highest evescape escape score (0.906) with fully neutral ESM-1v plausibility (1.0), so both escape and viability signals align.
Highest EVEscape score (0.906) with full PLM plausibility; MSA evidence has very low applicability (0.33) and reliability, so it only mildly tempers confidence.

Highest EVEscape escape score (z=0.906) with full PLM plausibility (z=1.0); low MSA applicability (0.33) limits the weight of the zero conservation evidence.
